headline: Stocks Eye a Second Day of Gains as Oil and UK Inflation Cloud the Open
body_html:
Wall Street heads toward Wednesday's open with some momentum after Tuesday's session, when 396 of the 544 stocks we track rose and 143 fell. Homebuilders led with an average gain of 2.95%, ahead of healthcare at 2.12% and software at 1.83%. Semiconductors and energy barely moved, at 0.09% and 0.15%.

The overnight backdrop is less comfortable. UK inflation climbed to 3.5%, its highest reading in almost a year, and a Bank of England policymaker warned that price risks are bigger than assumed. Oil is firmer on Middle East supply worries and falling US inventories, while Washington is nudging refiners to produce more diesel as prices climb.

At the open, watch energy-sensitive names and airlines, after United cut its 2026 profit outlook on fuel costs even as travelers kept booking. Also watch whether Tuesday's strength holds in healthcare and industrials, where Sarepta rose 8.12% and 3M gained 5.78%, while Mueller Industries fell 6.59% and Genuine Parts slid 5.12%. Iran-related diplomacy could move crude quickly.

briefs.headline: UK Price Pressures Re-Accelerate
briefs.body: British inflation rose to 3.5%, the highest in nearly a year, and a Bank of England official said the risks to prices are larger than previously thought. The data may temper hopes for easier policy and keeps rate expectations in focus for global investors this morning.

briefs.headline: Crude Firms on Supply Anxiety
briefs.body: Oil is higher as traders weigh Middle East supply fears and drawdowns in US inventories. Energy as a group gained only 0.15% on Tuesday, so any further climb in crude could test whether that sector finally catches up with the broader rally.

briefs.headline: Washington Presses Refiners on Diesel
briefs.body: US energy officials are encouraging refiners to raise diesel output as prices surge. Separately, North Dakota producers are speeding up well completions in response to higher prices, according to the state regulator. Together the moves show how quickly industry and government are reacting to tight fuel markets.

briefs.headline: United Trims Outlook on Fuel Costs
briefs.body: United Airlines lowered its 2026 profit forecast, blaming higher fuel prices, though it noted travelers are still booking despite pricier fares. Expect airline shares to trade with crude today, as demand looks resilient but costs are the swing factor for margins.

briefs.headline: Boeing Clears a Long-Awaited Hurdle
briefs.body: Boeing received FAA approval for its 737 Max 10 after years of delays, removing a significant obstacle for the narrow-body program. The news gives the aerospace group a constructive headline heading into the open, and investors will watch how the shares respond.

briefs.headline: Mediation Efforts Around Iran Continue
briefs.body: Iran says Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have yet to respond to its mediation offer, while a Qatari delegation has reportedly arrived in Tehran. Any sign of progress or a breakdown could shift oil prices and risk appetite, so geopolitical headlines remain a key swing factor at the open.
